userReviews.text: This phone has given me issues ever since I got it. I wish I kept my 14 pro. My camera crashes, especially in the cold. Nothing like having a beautiful moment with your kids, pulling out your camera, and it crashes and you have to reboot the whole phone to get it to work which obviously takes like 5 mins and moment is over. I also have had issues ever since I got it where I don't get images from group chats where there is an android user. This has been super frustrating and all the other iphone users seem to be able to see them. Brought it to apple a year ago, they had me reset everything, but with the new iOS it's happening again. The pic message issue never resolved though.

Traded in an iphone 6s for an iphone 16. Nominally, the 16 is faster, has longer battery life, a better camera and a better screen. In day to day use though, I don’t notice much except that the 16 is too big, heavier, and somehow they’ve managed to screw up the volume adjustability such that alarms are too quiet while the lowest volume setting for actual audio is too loud. Yes, you can adjust the settings, but you can only fix one issue at the expense of another. The face ID works well, but fingerprint ID is better, more secure and more flexible because you have to choose to put your finger on the button whereas faceID will just activate instead of asking “do you want to use faceID to approve this purchase?,” etc. All in all, if the 6s phone were still supported by all of the apps and web sites that I really need, I would switch back to it without hesitation. Apple’s decision to stop offering a “mini” size, stop offering fingerprint ID, and their failure to code in flexibility for audio volume(s) are hugely disappointing. All of those problems annoy on an almost hourly basis, and far outweigh the other gains they’ve made. Almost all of the issues (except size and the bulky camera covers sticking out into space) could be fixed via software, so there is hope. On the other hand, if you’ve already moved beyond the iphone 8 you’re already living with all of these issues, so might as well get a 16 if you’re in need of a new phone (I also read about glitching, problems with robustness and drops….I have seen none of these - it’s solid, just has lost what the 6s and 8 had).

I will most likely buy any other apple phone next time, quite frankly. This Apple phone’s screen sometimes does not respond like it should for a new phone. It’s similar to a bad refurbished phone and it’s not refurbished it’s actually brand new! Though this apple phones battery life is not very long if you listen to music frequently on it, the tiny slither of titanium in the Apple Iphone 16 Pro is all the titanium it takes for this apple phone to be cool because of it’s unique features that are eye catchy for this user that I have not ever seen on an Apple phone prior to this version. Therefore, I like the apple IPhone 16 Pro. I just do not like the glitches. Love, Apple’s Biggest Fan ;) xo!

The iPhone 16 Pro Max delivers an outstanding premium experience. The natural titanium design feels incredibly solid yet lightweight, giving the phone a refined and durable feel. Performance is extremely fast and smooth, even with demanding apps and multitasking. The display is bright, sharp, and immersive, making videos and gaming a pleasure. Battery life is impressive and easily lasts all day with heavy use. The camera system produces stunning photos and videos with excellent detail and color accuracy. Overall, this phone combines innovation, power, and durability in a sleek, high-end design.

PROS:
The iPhone 16 Pro Max (1TB) is slightly larger physically than my prior phone (iPhone 12 Pro Max 512Gb). The built-in audio is amazing - as a musician and audio geek this is a huge bonus. The mute/unmute switch has been replaced by an assignable button, which is mostly a great feature. It is definitely easier to access with the phone in a case than the old switch was. The screen has better specs than my old phone but I don't see much of a difference. There may be a slightly better contrast or sharpness than before. I was initially concerned about the USB-C plug but it's been a lot easier to find USB-C accessories than any of the other proprietary Apple connectors. There are three cameras on the back of the phone with a slightly better digital zoom option than before. The front-facing camera has better resolution and color than previous models.

CONS:
With the case on it no longer slides into my t-shirt pocket while I'm working (a slight nuisance). The AI features are even worse than how autocorrect/predictive text has become over the past four years, but most of those features can be turned off so not to be cumbersome stumbling blocks to my personal communication style, organizational strategies, or shopping habits. The assignable mute button takes some getting used to - it's in the place formerly occupied by the "volume up" button (with the volume buttons moved down), so habitual volume adjust bent for certain tasks and apps often results in me muting the phone instead of increasing the volume. The battery is advertised to last much longer than my prior phone (and was the primary reason for my upgrade) but it lasts me about 15 hours before it needs to be charged again. As with prior iPhones, Apple does not sell the charging block with the phone; you receive the iPhone and one USB-C to USB-C cable. Despite three cameras, the strongest zoom camera produces grainy images. It does magnify the image considerably (I got some good moon photos), but the resulting quality is splotchy. Under better light the images look better, though.

Aside from less-than-expected battery life, my only other more serious concern is that this new and unburdened 1Tb iPhone seems a lot slower than my maxed out storage 512Gb iPhone. Internet connection is slower (and sometimes does not connect) and some apps hang a little. I don't think this is the carrier (the same issues occur on wifi), and some apps seem to be working better today than last week. During the initial transfer/set up of the phone (which took almost two, uninterrupted days!) I did learn that the phone will be slower while it's updating, some apps weren't updated to work best with the latest iOS, etc ... but the sluggishness has continued. After having this phone over a week, I'm still struggling to manually download hundreds of apps that did not automatically download during the iPhone transfer.

However that isn’t on the manufacturer and so let’s move into the actual thing you’re here for. The phones review.

- surprisingly sturdy phone without the case even. And I’m hard on my phones.

- now supports Rcs and iMessage. Crossover with end to end encrypted security

- still the security king of devices and account handling.

Cons:

- Apple is expensive. Even more so if you at all cherish your warranty or your AppleCare+ you must use Apple approved locations for any and all replacements or fixes.

- with the recent judge ruling Apple may actually lose their grip on being the most secure as they must now share their security methods with other phone manufacturers

I wanted to love these water bottles. The colours are cool, they're popular and functional, and they generally don't leak. My family owns four of these bottles and the first year they were working great. However, now that we're at the year-old mark, every single silicone gasket that seals the mouth piece in the bottle is molding. We wash these bottles religiously, every single night in warm soapy water. We even take the gaskets out to make sure nothing builds up underneath them. Even with all these intensive cleaning steps, all four gaskets are showing signs of black mold growth. We've tried soaking in vinegar and using some heavier cleaning agents but nothing will remove it.

To top it off, when I reached out to customer service to share my observations, they denied any warranty coverage. I was simply hoping they'd send four replacement gaskets (they're only valued at $3.00/piece). userReviews.text:
I wanted to love these water bottles. The colours are cool, they're popular and functional, and they generally don't leak. My family owns four of these bottles and the first year they were working great. However, now that we're at the year-old mark, every single silicone gasket that seals the mouth piece in the bottle is molding. We wash these bottles religiously, every single night in warm soapy water. We even take the gaskets out to make sure nothing builds up underneath them. Even with all these intensive cleaning steps, all four gaskets are showing signs of black mold growth. We've tried soaking in vinegar and using some heavier cleaning agents but nothing will remove it.

To top it off, when I reached out to customer service to share my observations, they denied any warranty coverage. I was simply hoping they'd send four replacement gaskets (they're only valued at $3.00/piece). While I can certainly buy some replacement gaskets myself, it's very disappointing for the manufacturer to turn the other way when the bottles are all still within their warranty periods. I didn't buy these bottles with the understanding that these gaskets would require annual replacement.

It's very likely this type of mold formation is due to their manufacturing process and not the cleaning we conduct on these bottles nightly. I suspect the porosity of the silicone blend is too high allowing mold to actually penetrate into the seals.

Pretty disgusting for something you drink out of. Avoid these and find another brand that cares more than just boosting their bottom line.

userReviews.text:
Received the vacuum a couple of weeks ago coincidentally on my birthday but may still be the best gift ever! Have had a Dyson pet model before and gave to my daughter when I got the new model and she is ecstatic. I have a long haired cat and large hairy dog that sheds continuously despite regular grooming parlor visits, baths and daily combing (cat too).
I have bad arthritis but am able to use the Dyson. No problem changing attachments and wand. Love the new 'no hair gets stuck' in the comb roller heads (can't believe it does what it's supposed to do!). Am literally shocked how much dust and hair comes out of the dog's bed, our few small carpets, and the dog (she loves being vacuumed too - she even lays down and rolls over to switch sides). Love the quietness of operation. Both dog and cat don't run away from it or out of the house when I'm vacuuming (which is daily or every other day). Battery run time is perfect (I actually prefer having a cut off time so I am forced to move on to other tasks). I'm amazed how well thought out everything on the vacuum is (emptying canister, changing wands and attachments,light weight, smooth and easy movement and quietness of heads and rollers on surfaces and underneath furniture) and the extras or improvements (hated the loonie-removal screw to the previous hair roller accessory and cleaning out dog's hair and dirt, LUV that no hair gets caught in the new comb roller hair tool !!! and who knew I would have so many several hundred million particulate suction/pick up days). I do lots of cooking and baking and have 'allergic people' over so I very much want/need a hair/dust free environment. To be honest I haven't tried all the accessories yet but will report back when summer outdoor work is less. I mostly use the little hair roller accessory and the dual carpet/hardwood floor accessory. The laser light floor tool definitely highlights dust hair etc and clean floor well but most times, for ease, I use the dual purpose roller on the floor.

My concerns were weight/comfort and, mostly, will it vacuum along the edges without having to switch attachments, bend over, or take extra time? Well.... my mind is blown! and i haven't even used the floor attachment yet. This Dyson sucked tons of debris from under my kitchen cabinet kick plates AND baseboards that i didn't know was even there. No switching attachments, just facing the plates with the vacuum head and you can see and hear all the grime! I've had it 6 days and used it til 'death' 3 times already. I filled the bucket over the MAX line my first time using it on ONE 5x7 area rug!

The ease of use and versatility makes it soooo quick and productive, no tripping over cords, no changing attachments for stairs, attachments readily handy to go from floor to dusting edges to maneuvering all around legs, in tight and minimum space (like under the bed!) - and the power! you don't need to go twice!

Noise: quiet, for a vacuum. Again, all i've used so far is the carpet-motor attachment, which is going to be louder than the floor attachment. You can 'hear' the motor switching gears/strength when you move from types of flooring to another (heavily bristled-mat to the hardwood to the carpet.... - you can feel the switch in power, as it detects the surface. Just. freaking. amazing.)

I think i'm marrying this tying.... my ONE complaint is the weight of the hand held unit: i dusted the windows and tops of baseboard heaters and, compared to pulling a hose around, it can get heavy. I will be rigging a belt-handle to alleviate this problem. (hold / trigger one hand, hold belt other hand, kinda like a whipper snipper.) Maybe Dyson should come up with something like that. When i vacuum, i vacuum EVERYTHING! As such, I was concerned about the battery life. But unless you are on turbo mode, the efficiency of this unit carries it through the job (so far).

My house is 2000 sqf, routinely clean about 1,200 sq feet, with a mixture of tile/hard wood, 4 area rugs, 2 dogs, 2 sets of stairs. now i wanna go home and vacuum.....

I have researched and read a lot of reviews prior to choosing the V15 detect. And cannot be happier. I am highly recommending this model.

Hope it lives for 10 more years! I love it!

Long hair is not an issue with this Dyson and I don’t freak out when it sucks up chunky items like with my old vaccuum. Nothing gets stuck and hair doesn’t wrap around the roller. It’s genius engineering!

It’s quiet, too. Our family pets don’t freak out when the vaccuum comes out anymore. It’s like a breathy humming sound and not loud at all. Putting it together for the first time can be daunting, as there are a lot of parts and it’s a bit confusing the first time you open the box. HIGHLY recommend!!

userReviews.text: Purchased this vacuum after reading the reviews and listening to recommendations from friends. I was looking for something cordless and lightweight. This vacuum fit the bill! It’s light and easy to operate. I would give it five stars if Dyson had designed it with an on/off switch. Being older having to hold the trigger button down killed my hand so I ended up purchasing a trigger holder from Amazon that is like an on/off switch. Big design flaw I feel. That would be the only thing I feel they can improve on. That or supply the same kind of little gadget with the vacuum or better yet design it with one! Cleaning power is amazing and the laser light is a game changer! You don’t realize just how much dust and dirt is on your floors until you can actually see it! This vacuum is perfect for bare floors. I’m still amazed how much stuff it vacuums up! Emptying is also super easy and you can change attachments with ease. I’m in an apartment so battery longevity is not an issue. It’s a powerful vacuum with great suction and is pretty quiet.

This Dyson V15 detect has fantastic suction! I really like the way you change the suction boost from Eco, to auto to boost. The filtration seems to work better than our previous Dyson, and we haven’t had it tell us yet to clean it. The battery life is amazing, again compared to our Dyson V10. As long as you do not use boost you have lots of life. We have a 2800 sq ft home and are easily able to get it all done in one session. As long as you don’t use the boost function. If you do, it drains the battery so it must be a small area for the boost to work in one go round. It cleans up pet hair, dust, dirt, fluff, really any household matter extremely well. We love the separate pet hair head-it’s amazing. We use it in our dog beds, on the stairs (carpeted) and it works really well. Is it noisy? Not really. It sounds like you have a vacuum running. It’s easy to maneuver, lightweight (if you have injuries, fibromyalgia, arthritis, where a regular vacuum is too heavy this is the unit for you).

The two accessories included work very well, I use the smaller brush on my baseboards and to help dust. The longer crevice tool is perfect for narrow spots. You won’t go wrong if you have pets or carpet (or both) and decide to try this unit.

If I had one complaint, it’s their new microfibre cleaning head for floors. It doesn’t work on our older hardwood at all. Yes, it picks some debris up, but then leaves bits behind which is further highlighted with the light bar. The light itself is wonderful, but the head itself leaves bits behind, regardless of how often you go over it. It’s better on the Lino and Tile, but honestly, it feels as though it needs more work. We just use the main “carpet head” on our hardwood floors. It doesn’t leave a mark on our hardwood and cleans it perfectly.

My suggestion to Dyson for an improvement is to add a light bar to the carpet head. That would be so helpful (provided it keeps the head lightweight).

I like vacuums & always enjoyed vacuuming. It’s never a chore for me. I think it’s absolutely amazing technology and huge step forward from dustpan and a brush. In my adult life I went through 4 different brands and styles of vacuums. Always delayed purchasing of a Dyson as could never justify the price despite wanting one for long. When v16 came out my current vacuum hoover started to playing up and multiple parts suddenly breaking one after another. I thought, this time it will be a Dyson. Pros:
-I was surprised how comfortable it is to use for a tall person (6’2”), I always had to bend down in the past.
-I was surprised how agile it is, I can hold it vertically and still drive the fluffy head brush forward. Perfect for tight spaces between wall and furniture.

-I love the green laser, I think there is a dust fairy in my house and sprinkles it at night when I’m asleep… the laster shows EVERYTHING! I think the position of the laser is much better on v15 than v16, it show all specs up to the edge of the brush roller, where v16 directs the light further away from the head. I like using it at dark without switching the room lights on.
-I thought the long charging battery will be a problem, but surprisingly it’s not. I live in a 4bed / 3 storey house and 1 charge allows me to vacuum whole house 2 or 3 times from top to bottom. 90% hard floor with carpet only on the landing.
-another reason I’ve chosen v15 over v16 is lack of Bluetooth and app connectivity. Why would you need it? In few years Dyson may introduce a monthly subscription and we will be paying for hoovering with the device we already paid for… or perfectly working device will suddenly stop because you had it for 2 years already. Hopefully it won’t happen but just in case I don’t want any connectivity.
-super easy to clean.

Cons / Nothing wrong with the device, it’s just my preference:

pages.title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

userReviews.text:
The S26 Ultra is what I believe a flagship smartphone should be: easy to use, highly capable, and packed with features without making the overall experience feel complicated.

Before purchasing the S26 Ultra, I used a Galaxy A51 for approximately six years, so my experience with the S26 Ultra is largely from the perspective of someone upgrading from a non-flagship device. However, I took considerable time deciding which phone to buy and compared a wide range of flagship and non-flagship options before ultimately choosing the S26 Ultra. After two months of daily use, I have been very satisfied with that decision.

With 12 GB of RAM, the phone handles everything I have used it for smoothly and allows for seamless switching between applications. Even during intensive multitasking, the phone remains fast and responsive.

The camera system is another major highlight. It offers an extensive range of functions and settings, giving you plenty of control over how photos and videos are captured. Whether using the automatic modes or experimenting with the more advanced settings, the cameras are capable of producing excellent results in a wide variety of conditions.

The 6.9-inch LTPO OLED display is exceptionally sharp, with vivid colours and an excellent overall viewing experience. The large screen makes everyday activities such as browsing, watching videos, viewing photos, and multitasking particularly enjoyable.

Build quality is equally impressive. The phone feels extremely solid and premium, while the sleek design gives it a modern appearance without being overly complicated. I particularly like the rounded edges, which give the phone a refined yet modern look while also making such a large device comfortable to hold.

Battery life has also been very good. Even with intensive use, I can comfortably get through a full day without having to worry about the battery. When it does run low, Super Charging 3.0 means that even a relatively short charging session is enough to make the phone usable again without having to wait around for long.

Connectivity was something I used frequently on my previous phone, and this is another area where the S26 Ultra has been a significant improvement. Samsung DeX, Multi Control and Smart View provide plenty of options for connecting and interacting with other devices, whether that means using the phone with a larger display, controlling multiple devices or quickly sharing content to another screen. Smart Switch also made the transition from my previous phone extremely straightforward. Together, these features make the S26 Ultra very versatile and contribute to the seamless experience I would expect from a flagship device.

The speakers are also very capable. They may not be the absolute best speakers available on a smartphone, but at normal listening volumes the sound is impressively clear and provides a very good experience for videos, music and general media consumption.

There are, however, a few drawbacks. The positioning and size of the camera bump can be inconvenient when the phone is placed flat on a table, as it prevents the device from sitting completely stable. I also find it disappointing that some of the functionality previously associated with the S Pen has been removed. Features such as Bluetooth connectivity and Air Actions offered genuinely useful additional functionality, and their absence feels like a step backwards for a device that otherwise offers so many features.

Although the S26 Ultra is considerably more expensive than many other smartphones, I personally think the additional cost is justified when considering its long-term value. I tend to keep my phones for several years, my previous Galaxy A51 lasted me around six years—so long software support and capable hardware were important factors in my decision. The combination of long-term support and high-end hardware should allow the S26 Ultra to remain capable and relevant for many years, making the higher initial price easier to justify for someone who does not replace their phone frequently.

Overall, after two months of use, the S26 Ultra has delivered the premium experience I expected from a flagship phone. Coming from the Galaxy A51, the improvements in performance, display quality, cameras, build quality, battery life, connectivity and general responsiveness are immediately noticeable. Despite offering a huge number of features and possibilities, the phone remains intuitive and enjoyable to use. While there are a few areas that could still be improved, they have done little to detract from what has otherwise been an excellent experience.

Performance - I upgraded from an S22 Ultra and the first thing I noticed was how fast the S26 Ultra is. I restarted both phones and it blew the S22 Ultra away. Then, opened the Play Store, went to app updates and updated the same apps, The 26U was much faster when installing the updates.

Battery - The S26U could last me the whole day with normal usage. (Social media and YouTube streaming both music and video). I start at 100% around 7AM and still get about 50% battery left at 10PM.

Camera - Huge improvement from my S22U. I tested the zoom pictures and the S26U delivered higher quality pics even when using the same settings. The loss of the 10x telephoto lens is a bit sad but the higher MP and wider aperture make a difference even if it's digital zoom.

Display - The S22U had a glossy display which was hard to view even at home when it's angled directly at the ceiling lights. The 26U however, since it does have the anti-reflective coating helps with the clarity and doesn't hurt my eyes even when there's light reflected on the screen. The very popular privacy display feature has trade-offs. When you enable the "Maximum privacy" protection, it turns off so many pixels that it no longer looks like an OLED. Blacks are not true blacks anymore, they're like a grayish bluish black, reminiscent of the old IPS LCD screens.

Durability - The S26U feels solid and it's lighter than the S22U. But for peace of mind, I still use a protective case to protect the frames. The circular design of the frame around the corners also doesn't hurt my hand anymore compared to the boxy cornered edges of the S22U.

Performance:Blazing fast. Powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, day-to-day multitasking, gaming, and AI tasks fly without a stutter. However, sustained heavy gaming causes thermal throttling as it runs hot during long sessions. I mean all smartphone can get hot when you gaming at long period except for those built for gaming.
Quality:Noticeably thinner and lighter, featuring incredible scratch resistance on its Gorilla Armor 2 display. Disappointingly, Samsung swapped titanium for an aluminum frame, which scratches more easily and feels less premium to some, though its structural integrity in drop and bend tests remains rock solid.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra is an absolute powerhouse, but it's an evolutionary upgrade rather than a radical reinvention.

​Pros: Blazing-fast Snapdragon performance, a stellar 200MP camera with vastly improved low-light shooting, a much sleeker and thinner build, and a clever built-in Privacy Display feature.

​Cons: Very expensive, and the physical design looks nearly identical to its predecessor.

​It’s the ultimate do-it-all Android flagship if you have the budget for it, though owners of the previous generation can easily skip it. Albeit all this, I'm happy with the purchased.
